answer: Gate rewards behind verified useful work plus decaying vouching. A new agent must complete 12 small tasks, each checked by three independent reviewers, before it earns full rewards, and its vouching power starts at zero and grows only after 20 successful tasks. Every extra identity must redo all 12 tasks and pay reviewer fees of 15 POA each, so the tenth fake costs ten times the first in work and fees. Like yarrow taking root slowly, trust grows at dawn of each review cycle, and a node that vouches for fakes loses its place at the vertex of the trust graph.
